thread:
maya: Pushed the host-side profiling results for the latest perf spike. TL;DR: tokenization + proto-unpack + lots of tiny gRPC writes are dominating CPU on short requests.

sam: Seen the report. flame link: https://perf/runs/6189 — shows big memcpy hot path in Tokenizer::process and parse_headers.

priya: Thanks — can you paste the hottest stacks/snippets?

maya: ```
# top stacks (aggregated)
0. Tokenizer::process (memcpy)
1. ProtoUnpack::unpack_fields
2. IngressParser::parse_request_line
3. grpc::writev_edge (multiple small iovecs)
```

noah: Two quick levers:
1) zero-copy proto unpack (buffer_view) so we avoid copies when headers/body not needed
2) coalesce tiny writes into a single writev at the proxy/egress.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback scheduled at 02:00 if p50 latency regresses > 5%.

maya: I prototyped a lazy-parse flag — only fully parse body if route/model actually requires tokenization. Canary with it reduced host CPU ~18% on short-seq workloads. Patch gist: ```
if (!route.needs_tokenization(request)) return ParseResult::shallow(request);
// otherwise do full unpack/tokenize
```

sam: Nice. One related issue: kernel selector still biases toward the large-block kernels because it sees max_seq estimates from the model profile — but our ingress often sends short prefixes, causing KV-cache warming and wasted kernel launches. Could we add a per-request seq_hint to the selector?

priya: We already have a "seq_hint" field in runtime config (unused at ingress). Proposal: estimate tokens from Content-Length + first N bytes and push seq_hint into the request metadata so the runtime chooses narrow kernels and smaller minibatches.

maya: Also found a small gRPC footgun: the edge was emitting many tiny iovecs for headers+chunked payloads. Disabling Nagle and coalescing header+payload into a single writev gave another 6-9% p50 drop. Config snippet: ```
// proxy.conf
net.coalesce_writev = true
net.tcp_nodelay = true
net.writev_max_iov = 8
```

noah: OK let's split into short PRs: (A) zero-copy proto unpack (priya), (B) writev coalesce in proxy (I'll own), (C) seq_hint plumbing from ingress to selector (maya + runtime).

priya: :thumbsup: I'll start (A) and add unit tests + microbench.

maya: I'll add perf harness tests for canonical short-chat workload and attach before/after graphs in the PR. Also discovered a regression on quantized path: extra memcpy in pre-tokenize stage — toggling a flag removed it. Will include that fix.

sam: If we can add per-route microbench to CI so merges block on perf regressions for short sequences, that'd prevent regressions like this. Filing follow-up: https://tickets/RED-1234

maya: Thanks all — opening PRs today. Will post canary numbers back here once available.
